name: Balpakram National Park
description: National park in South Garo Hills known as the 'Land of Perpetual Winds' or 'Land of Spirits' in Garo folklore. Features dramatic canyons, plateaus, gorges, and dense forests. Home to elephants, red pandas, clouded leopards, wild water buffalo, and diverse birds. Part of UNESCO tentative Garo Hills Conservation Area.
facts: Established 1987, area about 220 km²
Elevation around 900-1000 m
About 60-70 km from Baghmara
Requires permit for entry; best Oct-March

name: Siju Cave (Dobakkol / Bat Cave)
description: One of India's longest limestone caves (about 4.7 km surveyed), famous for stalactites, stalagmites, underground streams, and large bat colonies. Located near Simsang River; popular for adventure exploration with local guides. Significant for biospeleology research.
facts: Third or among longest caves in India
First scientifically explored in 1922
About 30 km from Baghmara, 125 km from Tura
Guide essential; best Nov-March; entry fee low

name: Wari Chora
description: Hidden river canyon in South Garo Hills with turquoise waters of the Rongdik River flowing between tall limestone cliffs. Ideal for boating, kayaking, trekking, and photography in a remote, uncrowded setting. Name refers to 'land of the seven serpents' in local lore.
facts: Near Emangre village, about 2 hours from Baghmara
Requires off-road vehicle and local guide for last stretch
Best Oct-May; monsoon access difficult
Part of emerging Siju-Wari Chora-Baghmara circuit

name: Baghmara Pitcher Plant Wildlife Sanctuary
description: Small protected sanctuary near Baghmara town dedicated to the endangered endemic pitcher plant Nepenthes khasiana (locally Me'mang-Koksi). Located in reserve forest on the India-Bangladesh border area, with dense vegetation and occasional wildlife.
facts: Established 1984 for pitcher plant conservation
Very small area (~0.02-2.7 ha notified)
Near Baghmara town HQ
Also known as Baghmara Reserve Forest

name: Baghmara Town
description: District headquarters of South Garo Hills, a gateway town on the Simsang River near the Bangladesh border. Base for exploring Balpakram, Siju Cave, and Wari Chora. Known for local markets, Garo culture, and as entry to border reserve forests.
facts: HQ of South Garo Hills
About 110-130 km from Tura
Name from legend of tiger killed by local hero
Connected by road to Tura and Guwahati

name: Siju Bird Sanctuary
description: Small sanctuary across the Simsang River from Siju Cave, known for birdwatching including hornbills and peacock pheasants. Quiet riverside location ideal for early morning visits amid the Garo Hills forests.
facts: Near Siju Cave and Napak Lake
Good for migratory and resident birds
Accessible from Siju area
Part of local eco-tourism circuit
